_notes: Vanilla redstone scenarios, recorded by the asset generator's capture-scenarios (ScenarioCaptures.cs) on a headless vanilla server in a void world, whose game is frozen and stepped one tick at a time, with block states read with execute if block. Coordinates are absolute. Setup blocks are placed first, live, in order, with neighbor updates (/setblock). Each tick t from 1 to the scenario's ticks: its reloads (world saved and server restarted, which runs `ticks` game ticks of its own before the server is frozen again), actions, entity events (an armor stand standing in each contact cell until the next event) and arrows (flying straight into the face at the location, without gravity) happen first, at the previous game time, then the game advances one tick. Checkpoints hold the box after each tick: one string per (y, z) row, y then z ascending, with a character per x giving the block's palette index in 0-9a-zA-Z. Palette states are full states with every property, sorted by name.

scenarios.name: source_timing_lever
scenarios.description: A floor lever feeds a four-block dust line. The lever is on at tick 2, off at 6, on at 10 and off at 14, so the dust's on and off timing is observed at each change.

scenarios.name: dust_attenuation
scenarios.description: A 16-block dust line from a lever. Power falls by one per block; the lever is turned on at tick 2 and off at tick 20.

scenarios.name: repeater_delay
scenarios.description: Lever -> dust -> repeater (delay 2, input from the west) -> lamp. The lever is on from tick 2 to 10, so the repeater's delayed output is observed on both edges.

scenarios.name: repeater_lock
scenarios.description: A repeater (delay 2) at (2,1) is locked by a second repeater (delay 1, input from the north) at (2,0) that outputs into its side. The locking repeater is fed by a redstone block, placed at tick 1 and removed at tick 8. The lever is on at tick 3 and off at tick 12, so the lamp only responds once the lock is released.

scenarios.name: comparator_compare_and_subtract
scenarios.description: A comparator (input from the west, output to the east) with a rear block (15) and side dust at 14. Compare mode passes the rear value when it is at least the side value; subtract mode outputs the difference. The mode changes at tick 2, the side source is removed at tick 5, the rear source at tick 8, the mode returns to compare at tick 10 and the rear source is restored at tick 12.

scenarios.name: observer_pulse
scenarios.description: An observer (facing east) watches the block at (2,64,1). That block is placed at tick 2, removed at tick 6, placed at tick 10 and removed at tick 14; the observer's back powers a lamp.

scenarios.name: torch_inversion
scenarios.description: A standing redstone torch on a floor block that is itself swapped for a redstone block at tick 2 (the torch goes out) and back to stone at tick 6 (the torch relights). A lamp beside the torch follows it.

scenarios.name: torch_burnout
scenarios.description: The torch's support alternates between a redstone block and stone every two ticks from tick 1 to tick 33. A torch re-checks its support two ticks after a change, so each change toggles it, and rapid toggling burns it out: after that it stays off for the rest of the scenario.

scenarios.name: save_reload_repeater
scenarios.description: A repeater (delay 4, input from the west) is mid-delay when the world is saved and the server restarts at tick 3, so its scheduled tick must survive the reload. The lever is on at tick 2 and off at tick 8. Its chunks are force-loaded, so they load before the first tick after the restart.

scenarios.name: tripwire_line
scenarios.description: Two hooks on a stone support each, facing each other across three tripwire blocks. An armor stand touches the middle wire from tick 2 to tick 8 and is then killed. The wire powers at tick 2 and rechecks 10 ticks later (tick 12), when nothing touches it, so it releases then. The hooks follow it.

scenarios.name: target_arrow
scenarios.description: A target block on a stone floor with a lamp on its east side. The first arrow enters the west face off-centre at tick 2 and sets power 7. The second arrow enters at the centre at tick 5 while that pulse is pending, so it does nothing. The pulse ends 20 ticks after the first hit (tick 22), and the lamp follows the power.

scenarios.name: reload_target_pulse
scenarios.description: A target is hit at tick 2 (power 15, pulse due at tick 22). The world is saved and the server restarts at tick 10, while the pulse is still pending, so its remaining delay must survive the reload. The lamp beside the target follows the pulse.

scenarios.name: piston_extend_retract
scenarios.description: A normal piston faces east with a stone block in front. Power from a redstone block behind it extends it at tick 2 and removes the power at tick 12; the head retracts and the stone stays.

scenarios.name: piston_sticky_pull
scenarios.description: A sticky piston faces east with a stone block in front. Power on at tick 2 and off at tick 12; on retraction the stone is pulled back to the piston.

scenarios.name: piston_obsidian_blocked
scenarios.description: A powered piston faces east toward obsidian. The obsidian can't move, so the piston stays retracted.
